descriptors.definition: Entities apply Ind AS 116 starting from the annual reporting period beginning on or after April 1, 2019. The date of initial application represents the start of this annual reporting period when the entity first adopts the standard.
inclusion: Application of lease transition rules from the start of the reporting period
exclusion: Retrospective application prior to the designated inception date without chosen options
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from subsequent measurement rules by focusing exclusively on initial adoption timing.

descriptors.concept_name: Definition of a Lease Practical Expedient
descriptors.definition: Entities can elect a practical expedient to bypass reassessing whether ongoing contracts contain leases upon transition. This provision applies to all ongoing contracts collectively rather than individual selections.
inclusion: Exempting all existing contracts from lease definition reassessment at transition
exclusion: Selective application of the practical expedient to individual leases
nearby_distinctions: Differs from full reassessment requirements because it preserves historical classifications under older standards for existing agreements.

descriptors.definition: Lessees must transition to the standard using either the full retrospective approach or the modified retrospective approach applied consistently to all leases. The chosen method governs how prior periods and cumulative adjustments are reported.
inclusion: Application of either full retrospective or modified retrospective transition methods
exclusion: Mixing different transition approaches across individual lease contracts
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by whether comparative prior periods are fully restated or adjusted via opening retained earnings.

descriptors.concept_name: Modified Retrospective Approach for Operating Leases
descriptors.definition: Under the modified retrospective approach, lease liabilities are measured at the present value of remaining payments using the incremental borrowing rate. Right-of-use assets are measured either retrospectively or equal to the lease liability adjusted for prepayments.
inclusion: Measurement of remaining lease payments using the incremental borrowing rate
Adjustment of opening retained earnings for cumulative effects
exclusion: Restatement of comparative prior period financial figures
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with the full retrospective approach by avoiding prior period comparative restatements.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose specific policy details depending on whether they applied the full or modified retrospective transition approach. Required disclosures include the nature of the accounting change and weighted average incremental borrowing rates.
inclusion: Disclosures of financial statement line item impacts under full retrospective adoption
Explanations of differences in operating lease commitments under modified retrospective adoption
exclusion: Omission of transition adjustment explanations when practicable
nearby_distinctions: Varies based on the specific transition path chosen by the entity.

descriptors.concept_name: Lessor and Prior Sale and Leaseback Transition
descriptors.definition: Lessors make no transition adjustments except for intermediate lessors reassessing ongoing subleases based on head lease terms. Historical sale and leaseback transactions are not reassessed for sale criteria under newer revenue standards.
inclusion: Reassessment of operating subleases by intermediate lessors
Continuation of historical finance and operating leaseback accounting treatments
exclusion: Retrospective reassessment of historical sale qualifications under revenue standards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard lessors from intermediate lessors who must evaluate ongoing subleases against head lease right-of-use assets.

descriptors.concept_name: Sale and Leaseback and Business Combination Transitions
descriptors.definition: Historical sale and leaseback transactions remain unadjusted, with prior operating leasebacks adjusting right-of-use assets for off-market deferred gains or losses. Favourable or unfavourable operating lease terms previously recognized in business combinations are derecognized against right-of-use assets.
inclusion: Adjustment of leaseback ROU assets for deferred items
Derecognition of pre-existing business combination lease term assets or liabilities
exclusion: Retrospective adjustments to historical sale determinations
nearby_distinctions: Differs from new transactions by locking in historical classifications while only adjusting carrying amounts for specific deferred items.

descriptors.definition: Pre-existing assets or liabilities recognized for favourable or unfavourable lease terms from business combinations are derecognized on transition. Their carrying amounts are adjusted directly into the corresponding right-of-use asset.
inclusion: Derecognition of business combination lease intangibles
Offsetting adjustments to right-of-use asset carrying amounts
exclusion: Retaining separate intangible assets or liabilities for acquired lease terms
nearby_distinctions: Substitutes legacy business combination adjustments with direct modifications to the newly recognized right-of-use asset.

descriptors.definition: Published financial statement extracts illustrate practical balance sheet presentation formats for right-of-use assets and lease liabilities. These disclosures provide empirical reference points for corporate adopters.
inclusion: Illustrative balance sheet line items for listed entities
exclusion: Normative accounting rules or mandatory calculation formulas
nearby_distinctions: Serves as an illustrative disclosure exhibit rather than a standard measurement principle.

descriptors.concept_name: Key Differences Between Ind AS 17 and Ind AS 116
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 116 replaces risk-and-reward lease classification for lessees with a single control-based right-of-use model requiring asset and liability recognition. Exemptions are introduced for short-term leases and low-value asset leases.
inclusion: Single lessee accounting model for all qualifying leases
Exemptions for short-term and low-value leases
exclusion: Dual operating and finance lease classification for lessees
nearby_distinctions: Replaces the dual classification framework of older standards with a unified capitalization model.

descriptors.concept_name: Key Differences Between Ind AS 116 and AS 19
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 116 introduces comprehensive guidance centered on control and lease modifications, eliminating lessee lease classification found in older local standards. It also aligns sale and leaseback accounting with revenue recognition standards.
inclusion: Detailed control assessment guidance
Unified lessee accounting without operating and finance distinctions
exclusion: Deferral and amortization of sale and leaseback profits under older local rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes modern control-based accounting frameworks from older local accounting standards that relied on risk transfer classifications.

descriptors.concept_name: Major Changes Under Ind AS 116 from IFRS 16
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 116 incorporates specific national carve-outs from global standards, notably prohibiting fair value models for investment property right-of-use assets. Furthermore, it mandates that interest payments on lease liabilities be classified exclusively as financing activities.
inclusion: Mandatory financing activity classification for lease interest payments
Deletion of fair value measurement options for investment property right-of-use assets
exclusion: Operating activity classification options for lease interest payments
nearby_distinctions: Differs from international norms by enforcing rigid cash flow classifications and disallowing fair value options for investment properties.
